title: BEP · bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin
context_label: Ovarian dysgerminoma and other germ-cell tumours
schedule_label: Five consecutive infusion days, then bleomycin on days 8 and 15.
schedule_summary: Bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin are given on day 1. IV fluids and an anti-sickness plan cover the five-day cisplatin block. Return on each of days 2, 3, 4 and 5 for etoposide, cisplatin and fluids. Keep using the same dated anti-sickness prescription for this block. Bleomycin alone on days 8 and 15. The cycle repeats every 21 days. The consultant confirms your total number of cycles based on diagnosis and risk.
purpose: Treat the germ-cell tumour with curative intent.
indication_text: Includes advanced or metastatic ovarian dysgerminoma (00300c). Testicular and extragonadal indications have separate NCCP codes under the same protocol.
administration_text: Bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin are given on day 1. IV fluids and an anti-sickness plan cover the five-day cisplatin block. Return on each of days 2, 3, 4 and 5 for etoposide, cisplatin and fluids. Keep using the same dated anti-sickness prescription for this block. Bleomycin alone on days 8 and 15. The cycle repeats every 21 days. The consultant confirms your total number of cycles based on diagnosis and risk.
monitoring_summary: Review counts and tumour markers, renal and liver profile, chest X-ray and cumulative bleomycin.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Bleomycin
agents.explanation: It causes DNA strand breaks. Lung injury can develop during or after treatment.
agents.mechanism: It causes DNA strand breaks. Lung injury can develop during or after treatment.
agents.watch: Call urgently for new dry cough or breathlessness. Tell anaesthesia teams about past bleomycin.
visual: It causes DNA strand breaks. Lung injury can develop during or after treatment.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: It prevents dividing cells from rejoining DNA. Low blood counts and hair loss can follow.
agents.mechanism: It prevents dividing cells from rejoining DNA. Low blood counts and hair loss can follow.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, faintness or breathing difficulty during an infusion.
visual: It prevents dividing cells from rejoining DNA. Low blood counts and hair loss can follow.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing loss, reduced urine or new numbness.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Lung inflammation · Bleomycin
serious_effects.text: Report new cough or breathlessness immediately, including after treatment ends.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Call urgently with fever, shivering or unexplained bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Hair loss · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Ask the team about support before treatment.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team about ringing or new hearing loss before further cisplatin.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: IV fluids help protect the kidneys. Report reduced urine or persistent vomiting urgently.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: Five consecutive infusion days, then bleomycin on days 8 and 15.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shivering or sudden illness. Report new dry cough or breathlessness immediately, even after the last dose.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Ask about fertility preservation before the first dose.

evidence.title: Gynaecologic Oncology Group ovarian germ-cell study
evidence.interpretation: The study supports the activity of BEP after complete resection of ovarian germ-cell tumours.
evidence.limitations: This was an adjuvant study. Its outcomes cannot be used to estimate an individual response in unresected or metastatic disease.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before day 1
cells: Blood count, renal and liver function, germ-cell markers, chest assessment, lung function and hearing as indicated.
Ask about fertility preservation before the first dose.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: Review counts and tumour markers, renal and liver profile, chest X-ray and cumulative bleomycin.
Tell the team about any cough or change in exercise tolerance before the next dose.

rows.label: During infusions
cells: Review hydration, urine output, magnesium and other salts, hearing and nerve symptoms.
Tell the nurse promptly about chills, rash, swelling or trouble breathing.

monitoring_schedule.note: Scan dates and tumour-marker testing are individualised by your oncology team.
